paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/17/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 23:57 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 49.65 and Kalshi 53.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 11/12, she is first in all 67 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 27% to 38%, and leads in the 32 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 17.7 across 36 lists from 5 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 61 of the 67 lists of the last 45 days; in the 11 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 25 of the 67 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 17.85, and at 15.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he does not place in the top two in any of his 25 lists and averages 8.1 across 18 lists from 5 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 4th on Polymarket, at 5.95, and at 5.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are by Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 11/09 and 11/10, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 11/09, is at 1.85 on Polymarket and 2.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 2 of the 67 lists, at 2% in the Cluster17 one and 4% in the OpinionWay one for CNews, with fieldwork from 11/10 to 11/12. The Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, with fieldwork on 11/12 and 11/13, which also tests him, already has an official notice and is not yet in the database.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than double Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 13.3 over the last 30 days, across 26 lists from 5 pollsters, and Glucksmann 12.4, across 34 lists from 5 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 3 of 46, and Glucksmann in 3 of 62. In the win contract, Philippe is at 4.50 on Polymarket and 5.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.85 and 3.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 11/17, four of the ten headlines, from 9 outlets, are about the primary of the right and the centre.** franceinfo reports that the campaign directors of Gabriel Attal, David Lisnard and Bruno Retailleau met on 11/17 and that, according to Attal's entourage, the three accepted the first rules: a two-euro participation fee, mostly electronic voting, a commitment to refuse "any alliance with the extremes" and two rounds in January, with two possible sets of dates still open; according to franceinfo, Édouard Philippe refuses to take part. Europe 1 and CNews report the three's agreement on a primary in January; in an earlier headline, at 17:05 UTC, Ouest-France spoke of a deadlock. 20 Minutes and Libération report that Unicef France has suspended Teddy Riner's ambassador mission; in a statement to AFP, the organization says the decision is meant to preserve its neutrality. Le Parisien reports that Dominique de Villepin will announce his decision on 2027 at a press conference on Friday, 11/20. Les Echos runs an analysis according to which Marine Le Pen wants her pension reform to appeal to both the financial markets and working-class voters, and a piece on the campaign in bookshops, from Jordan Bardella to Jean-Luc Mélenchon; BFMTV runs a video asking whether the campaign is a communication war.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
